summary.headline: Pennar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3.6% to INR884.55 crore while PBT grew 16% to INR46.8 crore, with PBT margin at 5.38%.
summary.overview: Revenue growth was moderate as legacy steel, railways and diversified businesses shrank, but EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR106.8 crore and PBT rose 16% to INR46.8 crore. Management attributed margin gains to mix shift toward PEB US and engineering services, though PEB India margins dropped for a month or two due to delayed steel pass-through. Order books are at record levels in PEB India (INR1,008 crore), PEB US (above USD100 million) and boilers (INR150.75 crore), while Hydraulics orders softened on US tariff uncertainty. Management guided to double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth in Q2 and reiterated a 7% PBT margin target over about three years. Questions on segment EBITDA, employee cost growth, other income and the promoter warrant issue drew deferred or defensive answers.

segments.name: PEB India
segments.commentary: Order book at record INR1,008 crore; execution hit by engineering clearance and delivery issues, and PEB margins fell over 200 bps for a month or two until steel price increases were passed through. Management expects margins to recover from Q2.

segments.name: PEB US (Ascent)
segments.commentary: Order backlog crossed USD100 million (about USD70 million cited in one answer as the prior-quarter level), revenue running ahead of plan; US revenue stream described as the highest-margin unit with operating margins above 15%.

segments.name: Engineering Services (structural engineering, BIM)
segments.commentary: Structured engineering grew 26.3%; annual revenue about INR70 crore, mainly US and Europe. Management says productivity gains of 30-35% are being used against AI-driven automation risk.

segments.name: Boilers
segments.commentary: Order backlog at record INR150.75 crore; first industrial power boiler achieved as pre-qualification reference, and first pharmaceutical-sector orders won.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR30 crore; US activity slowed on tariff uncertainty while Europe performed well. Management is in wait-and-watch mode; the business is about INR100 crore a year.

segments.name: Tech Pennar
segments.commentary: Named as the weak spot: thin order book and execution issues at some customers; a new sales team is in place with improvement expected from Q2.

segments.name: BIW (body-in-white)
segments.commentary: Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026 with three programmes; management expects revenue to double over the next three months on a scheduled order basis.

segments.name: Legacy businesses (steel, railways/Cadnum, tubing)
segments.commentary: About INR1,300 crore annual revenue, now about 25% of group revenue and declining; capital is no longer being deployed and management is seeking a value-realisation structure similar to the solar JV with Zetwerk.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27: double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth expected; PEB margins expected to return to prior levels from Q2.
FY27: management says 20% PAT growth is the stated goal for the year; ROCE target about 25-30% for the year (Q2 above 20%).
Debt-to-equity target about 0.7 by year-end FY27; management says anything above 0.7 is unacceptable, with INR20 crore of the promoter's INR50 crore commitment already in.
Over three years PBT margin target of about 7%, from 5.38% now.
Management said it expects the combined entity to grow at double-digit rates from Q2 as higher-growth units scale, while legacy units decline.
capex_capacity: PEB India capacity is available, but execution was hit by engineering clearance delays and labour constraints, which management says are resolved.
PEB US and India advance payments fell to about 25% from 5-10% earlier, as the company moved to reduce working capital.
BIW Hyundai plant commissioned in August 2026; three programmes in place.
Management is deliberately building raw-material inventory ahead of expected PEB revenue, which weighed on working capital.
Management is not deploying capital into legacy businesses (steel, railways, Cadnum aerospace); no material capex.
demand_pricing: Record order books across PEB India, PEB US and boilers; the company says the larger backlog is now ready to execute.
Hydraulics bookings below expectations on US tariff uncertainty; Europe performed well.
Steel price pass-through was delayed for about 1-2 months, which compressed PEB margins.
Management says it has about 6-7% share of an addressable market of INR2.25-2.3 lakh crore, and an obtainable market of about INR80,000 crore.
Solar JV with Zetwerk: Pennar holds 45% of a 2 GW capacity entity with potential revenue of about INR4,000 crore; no current revenue numbers were disclosed.
